findings.title: Transaction wrapper does not own storage failures

evidence.detail: Body failures are rolled back but re-raised unchanged.
Commit occurs outside the rollback handler.

findings.impact: Storage errors can lack operation_id; commit failure can leave an active transaction.
findings.remediation: Handle body and commit failures, roll back, and translate SQLite errors.

findings.title: Money validation exceeds SQLite's integer domain
findings.impact: Large amounts can overflow outside the stable model.

findings.title: CSV import has no resource bound

evidence.detail: The entire parsed CSV is materialized.
Import also retains all seen rows.

findings.impact: Large CSV can exhaust memory in a transaction.

report.security_posture: Parameterized SQL and no credentials; unbounded CSV permits local exhaustion.
report.strongest_quality: State and audit writes share explicit transactions.
report.weakest_quality: Storage failures are neither recovered nor normalized.

evidence.detail: Import validation, writes, audit, and result share one method and transaction.
Public operations are direct and named.
Class contains only ledger persistence and transitions.
Import identity is constrained but numeric/reversal bounds are not.
CSV parsing is short and native.
Tests omit storage, concurrency, and size failures.
Transaction boundary cannot own every storage failure.

overall_readiness.rationale: Core behavior works, but storage-failure ownership blocks production.

take_production_ownership.rationale: Compact and auditable after failure boundaries are hardened.

test_confidence.supplied: Four tests establish normal persistence, validation, import rollback, reconciliation, reversal, and closure.

input_boundaries.detail: Numeric and CSV bounds are open.

secrets.detail: No credential threat model was supplied.

observability.detail: Business audit exists but storage errors lose operation context.

settings.tools: read candidate; run only supplied sandbox command
